Notes, Pages, Slides and Sheets

Four kinds of document, one library — start from a template and learn what each is for.

#Which kind should I use?

Notes for thinking, Pages for documents, Slides for presenting, Sheets for numbers. All four live in All docs, in folders, and on every page that lists documents.

  1. New (top left) or the + button creates any kind; folders can hold all four.
  2. On All docs, the pills Notes · Pages · Slides · Sheets filter the library; each kind has its own icon and tile shape.
  3. Pages, Slides and Sheets are stored as real .docx, .pptx and .xlsx files, so they open in other apps too.
  4. Open a .docx, .pptx or .xlsx from the Files page to edit it in place; Save writes back to the same file.

Tip Not sure? Start with a Note. You can convert it to a Page later with “Convert to a Page…”.

#Start from a template

A gallery of ready-made starting points for every kind.

  1. Press Ctrl+Shift+N, or New → From template…, or use the Create button on All docs.
  2. Pick Notes, Pages, Slides or Sheets (Alt+1 to Alt+4), search, and press Enter or click a card.
  3. Pages: letter, résumé, report, handbook, project proposal, meeting minutes, one-page brief, press release, procedure, weekly report. Slides: briefing, lesson, pitch, field notes, quarterly report, evening talk. Sheets: household budget, quarterly sales, gradebook, project tracker, invoice, weekly timesheet, habit tracker.
  4. Everything in a template is ordinary content — change it freely. Save your own note templates from ••• → Save as template….

#Pages: real documents

Type like in a word processor; the panel on the right holds styles, fonts, paragraph, insert, page setup, review and view.

  1. Click the page and type. Use the toolbar for style, font, size, bold, lists and colours.
  2. Open the panel (right icon in the toolbar) → Page for paper size, orientation and margins; Insert for tables, pictures, headers, footers and page numbers.
  3. Ctrl+F finds text; Review has spelling, comments and tracked changes.
  4. ••• → Export as… saves a PDF, Word, Markdown, HTML or text copy wherever you choose.

Tip Every command of the engine is reachable: the ⋯ at the end of a panel group and Ctrl+/ (command search) list them all.

#Slides: build and present

A slide rail on the left, the slide in the middle, speaker notes underneath and a panel on the right.

  1. Click + New slide (or the arrow beside it for a layout). Click a slide in the rail to edit it; drag to reorder.
  2. Click on the slide to select; double-click text to type. Drag handles to resize. Insert shapes, pictures, tables and charts from the toolbar.
  3. Design tab: themes and variants. Motion tab: transitions and animations.
  4. Press Present (or F5) for the slide show: arrows or click to advance, Esc to leave.
  5. Write speaker notes in the pane below the slide.
  6. ••• → Download as PowerPoint… or Export as PDF… saves a copy wherever you choose.

Tip Pick a starter from the template gallery — each one comes with sample slides and a matching theme.

#Sheets: numbers, formulas and charts

A grid with a formula bar, sheet tabs, a status-bar summary and a panel with every spreadsheet command.

  1. Click a cell and type; Tab and Enter commit and move. = starts a formula; the formula bar suggests functions.
  2. Drag the fill handle (the small square at a selection’s corner) to copy or continue a series; drag column and row edges to resize, double-click to fit.
  3. Select cells, then Insert → Chart. Click a chart to move it; the panel has chart design.
  4. Home has number formats, borders, fills and conditional formatting; Data has sorting, filters and validation (drop-down lists); Insert → Checkbox makes tick boxes.
  5. The status bar shows the sum, average and count of what is selected. The slider sets the zoom (or pinch).

Tip Unsure how a function works? Type = and its first letters, or use Ctrl+/ to search every command.

#Split view: two or three documents side by side

Read one document while you write in another, like editor groups in VS Code.

  1. Open two or more documents, then press the split button at the right of the tab strip (or Ctrl+\). The most recent other tab appears beside the current one. With only one tab open it asks which document to put beside it.
  2. Or right-click a tab → “Open beside the current document”.
  3. Each pane has a coloured bar and a number; the tabs showing in a pane carry the same colour and number, so you can see which tabs belong together. The pane you last clicked is the active one — the toolbar, breadcrumbs and ••• menu follow it.
  4. Drag the divider between panes to resize it (or focus it and press ← →). Click × on a pane header to close just that pane — the document stays open in its tab.
  5. A third pane is the most. Clicking a tab that is not showing replaces the document in the pane you are working in.

Tip Each pane starts with its format panel closed so the page has room; open it from that pane's toolbar when you need it.

#Spelling, grammar and AutoCorrect

Red dotted lines mark spelling, blue ones grammar; right-click for suggestions. Typos fix themselves as you type.

  1. In Notes, a misspelt word gets a red dotted underline and repeated words, a missing capital or “a/an” mistakes get a blue dotted one. Right-click the word (or press Alt+Enter with the cursor in it): its fixes appear at the top of the one menu — click a suggestion to replace the word, or choose Ignore all / Add to dictionary. Click anywhere else, or press Esc, to close it. Slides and Sheets show the same fixes when you right-click a word you are typing in a text box or a cell.
  2. AutoCorrect works when you finish a word: common typos (teh → the), a lone i → I, and a capital letter at the start of a sentence. Pages and Slides have their own AutoCorrect, which is on every time you open them; Pages also draws spelling and grammar marks.
  3. Turn the marks on or off in ••• → Spelling & grammar.

#Open a file with another app

Right-click a file or document to open it with any app that can read it.

  1. On the Files page, right-click a file → Open, or Open with and pick an app from the list (macOS and Linux list the apps that can open that type; Windows opens its own “Open with” window). “Choose another app…” always works.
  2. Files that Doceo can’t edit (images, archives, code…) open in the app your system uses for them when you click them.
  3. Right-click a Page, Slides or Sheet in the library → “Open a copy with…”. It opens a copy of the file in the other app; what you save there does not come back into Doceo.

#Pop out, tabs and saving

Open any document in its own window; edits save by themselves.

  1. Pull a tab out of the tab strip to open that document in its own window; drop it back on the strip to dock it.
  2. Pages, Slides and Sheets save into your library a moment after you stop typing (Autosave is always on). A document opened from the Files page is a draft until you press Ctrl+S, which writes the original file.
  3. Closing a tab with unsaved changes to a file asks Save / Don’t save / Cancel.
